Figure1: Figure 1. Model-guided solvent screening and prediction. (a) The Gaussian process (GP) model was fitted to 30 measurements, and expected improvement (EI) guided three rounds of five experiments. The curves show initial GP distributions of mean PE conversion in CHCl3 (blue) and CCl4 (orange). (b) Five-fold evaluation repeated ten times gives 450 test predictions for 45 solvents. Pale points show individual predictions, larger points show each solvent’s mean prediction, and the dashed line marks equality. Blue, purple and teal denote halogenated, amide and other solvents, respectively. (c) The ten candidates with the highest initial EI scores are shown. Points show predicted means, whiskers indicate 90% prediction intervals for measured conversion, and bars show EI. Filled symbols mark first-round selections; correlations between predictions can alter selection order. (d) The GP was compared with eight regression models used by Li et al22. All models used the same training and test solvents. Bars and whiskers show mean absolute error (MAE) and sample standard deviation (SD) across ten repeats; Ridge and linear KRR share a row. (e) Training sets of 18, 27 and 36 solvents were used to predict the same nine test solvents. Each larger training set contains the smaller one. Thin lines show the results of individual repeats. The thick line shows the mean across the ten repeats, and error bars show the sample SD. (f) For each pair, both solvents were excluded from the 45-solvent dataset, and their conversions were predicted using the other 43 solvents. Squares show measurements, open circles show predictions, and lines connect the two values for each solvent. PE denotes polyethylene, and R2 is the coefficient of determination. MAE, EI and SD are expressed in percentage points (pp). The model abbreviations kNN, SVR and KRR denote k-nearest neighbors, support vector regression and kernel ridge regression, respectively. DCA, TCA, TeCA, PentaCA, PCE, TCE and NMF denote dichloroethane, trichloroethane, 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane, pentachloroethane, tetrachloroethene, trichloroethene and N-methylformamide, respectively. X denotes Cl, Br or I.
Figure_M1: Figure M1. Predictions and measurements for three screening rounds. Each panel shows five solvents in recommendation order; Gaussian process (GP) models are fitted to 30, 35 and 40 solvents, respectively. Open circles show predictions before each round; filled squares show measured polyethylene (PE) conversion; whiskers show 90% prediction intervals for measured conversion (Section M5). Conversions are in %. Table M7 gives uncertainty (standard deviation) in the predicted mean and expected improvement (EI) used for selection, after accounting for correlations within each batch.
Figure_M3: Figure M3. Predicted conversion, uncertainty and initial solvent selection. (a) Gaussian process (GP) predictions for 229 candidates from 30 initial measurements. Axes show polyethylene (PE) conversion and uncertainty in its predicted mean (standard deviation, SD); color shows expected improvement (EI), the expected gain above 88.2% with a 100% conversion ceiling. Orange rings mark first-round selections; labels show initial ranks, with ranks one and two overlapping. (b) Top-ten candidates, structures and predicted means. Whiskers show 90% prediction intervals for measured conversion; bars show EI. Filled symbols, solid bars and bold names mark first-round selections. The last column shows selection order accounting for prediction correlations. pp, percentage points.
Figure_M4: Figure M4. Grouped Shapley contributions to Gaussian process (GP) predictions. Rows list the 45 solvents; columns show element counts, carbon/halogen environments, donor and functional groups, and bond-presence indicators. Each cell averages ten signed contributions from models fitted without that solvent’s response. Blue positive and orange negative values raise and lower predictions relative to the training background. Each fit uses 36 training molecules as background; four groups are retained or replaced with background values, giving 2⁴=16 combinations. Background plus four contributions equals the GP mean before limiting it to 0–100%. At right, squares show measured polyethylene (PE) conversion; open circles show the mean of ten predictions for each solvent, each prediction bounded to 0–100%; lines connect them. NMP, N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone; HMPA, hexamethylphosphoramide; DMSO, dimethyl sulfoxide; DMF, N,N-dimethylformamide; pp, percentage points. X=Cl, Br or I.
